Hero.name: Muhammad Naufal Arif
Hero.about: I work on quality assurance for AI training data and web systems. I started by auditing datasets and labeling 3D point clouds, then moved into building web applications. I pay attention to the details most people skip, because that is usually where problems start.

qa.title: Specialization
qa.description: Checking data before it is used. From annotation to audit, I make sure the result is correct, consistent, and can be trusted.

web.title: Web Development
web.description: Building applications from the server side to the interface.

gpa.title: Education
gpa.description: Information Systems graduate, STT Terpadu Nurul Fikri.

jobs.description: I am the final check on a Tier-1 autonomous driving dataset. Most of my time goes into auditing 3D LiDAR point clouds and making sure object boundaries are accurate. The work taught me that a model can only be as good as the data it learns from.
I labeled 3D point clouds into more than 40 object categories and checked that spatial boundaries did not overlap. This was the groundwork for the QA role that followed.
My first role in AI data. I tracked dynamic objects and traffic signs across 4D spatio-temporal datasets. Object IDs had to stay consistent from frame to frame, so small mistakes mattered.
Before moving into tech, I worked in operations. I checked company documents against records and monitored stock movement across branches. It trained me to spot discrepancies early.
I built a point-of-sale system from scratch for a local egg distributor, using Node.js and SQLite. It was my first time turning messy business requirements into a tool people use every day.
I taught Arabic grammar (nahwu and sharaf) and handled academic administration. Teaching taught me to explain complicated things in simple terms.

lidar.title: 3D LiDAR Spatial QA
lidar.desc: I audited and annotated 3D point clouds for autonomous driving datasets. Keeping spatial boundaries strict meant catching small errors before they reached the training data.

dialectica.title: Dialectica
dialectica.desc: A digital library built with Next.js. Users can ask questions about the books they read, powered by the Gemini API. The hardest part was keeping the AI's answers relevant over long conversations.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce Product Catalog
ecommerce.desc: A freelance project where I helped build a product management system. We used Laravel 12 and Livewire to keep the interface reactive without writing much custom JavaScript.

uwais.title: Uwais Point of Sale
uwais.desc: The first enterprise tool I designed and built. It handles invoicing and inventory tracking. Keeping queries fast on a local SQLite database was the main challenge.

kostku.title: Kostku Property Finder
kostku.desc: I worked as the project manager on this one. We built a property search interface with React.js. It showed me how Agile cycles work in practice, and why talking with designers matters as much as writing code.

forum.title: Discussion Forum API
forum.desc: A backend project. I wrote a REST API for a discussion forum with user authentication and nested comments.

rental.title: Car Rental System
rental.desc: A database-driven application for managing rental periods and user sessions, built with CodeIgniter.

ai.title: Data Infrastructure
ai.desc: 3D LiDAR mapping, semantic segmentation, bounding box tracking, and data quality audits.

web.title: Web Development
web.desc: TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, and Laravel.

data.title: Storage and Deployment
data.desc: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Git, and Vercel.

cert.title: Workflow
cert.desc: Agile, quick prototyping, and reading documentation carefully.
